newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fischler insists on cut in EU cereals aid.
newsitem.headline: Fischler insists on cut in EU cereals aid.

text.p: EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Tuesday that he will press ahead next week with a proposal to cut aid to cereals and oilseeds farmers to help fund assistance for beef farmers hit by the mad cow crisis.
The proposal is attached to the 1997/98 (July/June) farm price package which is due to be wrapped up by farm ministers at a meeting in Luxembourg between June 23-25.
The proposed cut in cereals aid is the most contentious item in the modest package of mainly unchanged prices.
"Yes, I will do it," Fischler told Reuters after appearing before the European Parliament's agriculture committee.
Asked if there would be any backing down given that nearly all 15 EU countries opposed the proposal, Fischler said, "No."
EU farm ministers are likely to seize on a recent Commission report showing a 2.0 billion Ecus budget saving in 1997 and that the arable aid cut is no longer necessary.
In a working paper, the Commission's agriculture directorate general estimated that EU cereal farmers have been over-paid by 8.46 billion Ecus during the past four seasons.

An earlier British study put the over-payments at 14.3 billion. The payments were intended to compensate farmers for cuts in intervention prices agreed under a 1992 reform of the Common Agricultural Policy.
But since then market prices have soared and farmers have been paid for losses they never suffered.
